evals.name: checks-without-touching-settings
evals.prompt: /context-guard:setup check
evals.expected_output: Reports jq, node and the zones.json state from the pre-computed context block rather than re-issuing those probes, reports whether the mod runs in this session, runs the retired-tee detector, reports live-session snapshot freshness against the 10-minute staleness rule and every option's effective value, and edits nothing.
expectations: Cites the pre-computed values verbatim as the evidence for the jq, node and zones.json findings: the resolved path or 'absent', and the zones.json contents or its absent/unreadable token
Reports the module row from its own tool list (mcp__context-guard__status present or absent) and `claude --version` against the 2.1.287 floor
Runs the retired-tee detector's three steps (stamps against the install record, cached versions holding a tee, wiring routes) and reports each finding
Reports a row for each of the 8 options, from context_guard_hooks_enabled to context_guard_band
Reads settings only; never writes settings, pluginConfigs, the snapshot directory or zones.json
Reports PASS/FAIL/INFO with one remediation line per FAIL

evals.name: reads-null-fields-as-expected-state
evals.prompt:
/context-guard:setup check

The live session's snapshot is fresh but used_percentage is null.
evals.expected_output: Reports the fresh-but-null snapshot as INFO: the documented state before the session's first response or right after /compact, in which the resolver correctly answers unknown, not a failure to fix.
expectations: Classifies null used_percentage / current_usage on a fresh snapshot as documented fail-open behavior
Does not tell the operator to rewire or reinstall anything for it
Cites the reader contract as the owner of the fail-open rule

evals.name: apply-preserves-unrecognized-keys-and-custom-bands
evals.prompt:
/context-guard:setup apply

My zones.json already exists with custom valid bands (40/70) and carries a custom display_color key another tool of mine reads.
evals.expected_output: Bare apply is repair-only: leaves the valid custom bands (40/70) untouched and reports them, preserves the unrecognized display_color key and its value (semantic preservation: lexical formatting may normalize), names 'apply defaults' as the explicit route to the shipped defaults, and confirms a second identical apply would be a no-op.
expectations: Writes only ~/.claude/context-guard/zones.json and nothing else (a fully valid zones file may mean no write at all)
Does NOT overwrite valid custom band values on a bare apply; names apply defaults as the explicit shipped-defaults mode
Preserves unrecognized keys rather than rewriting the file from the template
States idempotency (second run = no content change)

evals.name: uninstall-order-unwire-before-delete
evals.prompt:
/context-guard:setup check

How do I back this out completely? I want to remove the plugin and everything it put on my machine. My statusLine command is still: bash ~/.claude/context-guard/bin/statusline-shim.sh ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh
evals.expected_output: Says uninstalling the plugin stops the module and leaves ~/.claude/context-guard/ in place, and that, because a statusLine still names the shim, the unwire edit comes first (statusLine.command becomes ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh) and removing ~/.claude/context-guard/ comes second.
expectations: States the order explicitly and gives the reason: deleting the directory first leaves the status line invoking a missing file, so bash exits 127 and the whole status line goes down
Prints the edited statusLine.command as ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh, the person's renderer unchanged
Says the directory can be removed at any time once no statusLine names the shim, and that readers then read unknown
Edits nothing itself

evals.name: unwire-both-shims-before-a-renderer
evals.prompt:
/context-guard:setup check

I just updated context-guard. My ~/.claude/settings.json has statusLine.command set to: bash ~/.claude/context-guard/bin/statusline-shim.sh bash ~/.claude/rate-limit-guard/bin/statusline-shim.sh ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh
evals.expected_output: Reports the shims as a wiring route of the retired tee and prints the unwire edit: statusLine.command becomes exactly ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh in ~/.claude/settings.json, with both guards' shims removed. Also prints the leftover files to delete and the restart step, and edits nothing.
expectations: Prints the edited value as exactly: ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh
Removes the rate-limit-guard shim too, because both tees retired in the same release
Names ~/.claude/settings.json as the file to edit and does not edit it
Tells the person to restart sessions and lanes started before the update

evals.expected_output: Prints the unwire edit with only the shim pair removed: statusLine.command becomes exactly sh -c 'THEME=dark my-statusline --flag'. The sh -c layer stays, and the skill edits nothing.
expectations: Prints the edited value as exactly: sh -c 'THEME=dark my-statusline --flag'
Keeps the sh -c layer and its quotes rather than peeling it to the bare command
Does not edit settings.json itself
